title: The dashboard tool's honest result, and a narrow-terminal band with an [Open] Button
description:
opum-doc seq 182 item 3 (ODOC-OP-2026-10-03-13), relayed by opum-agent 2026-10-03 and binding for lore's 0.13.0 tool:
- The tool result must be honest. After opening, check $.ui.panes() and report what actually happened: "opened" only if the pane is shown; otherwise say it is waiting for a terminal at least 144 columns wide.
- On a narrower terminal, also show a one-line band above the prompt ("... ready") with an [Open] Button (hotkey o). A person's press seats the pane at any width; a model-originated open cannot.
- FIRST measure that a band Button press does seat the pane below 144 columns, and report if it does not.

Seq 183 (ODOC-OP-2026-10-03-14): intent routing is accepted as built -- dashboard with modifiers is the documented form, a word with no CLI meaning may route to the pane by obvious intent, but a real CLI command word goes to the CLI and never the pane. Keep that case in the live-session probe; do NOT add a probe asserting a non-CLI word reaches the CLI (it gates on model wording and is flaky).

PARKED at the 2026-10-03 team boundary so the fleet restart is not held: not started. LCLI-668 (the tool itself) is complete and merged; this is the follow-up increment.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Measured first, in a live session at a width below the floor, on the Claude Code version named in the evidence: a band Button press answers { isPlaced: true } and the pane draws, where the same pane opened unasked (at session start AND by a model tool call) answers { isPlaced: false, reason } and draws nothing. The evidence names the version, the width, and both answers verbatim; a measurement that does not hold is reported rather than worked around.

mcp__opum-lore__dashboard reports what actually happened, not what it asked for: it says the pane opened only when the engine has it placed AND shown; when the open waits undrawn it says so and carries the engine's own reason (which names the floor and the width now) rather than a hard-coded 144 columns; and a pane placed behind another pane's tab is reported as open behind a tab rather than as either of those. A test covers the placed and the waiting arms, with the placed case as the positive control that proves the waiting answer is the state's doing and not a message that always reads the same way. AMENDED before check-off: the behind-a-tab arm is read from $.ui.panes, and the engine's test kit carries no such call at all -- measured on it, "$.ui.panes is not a function" -- so no unit test can hold that arm; it rests on the live measurement instead, and the kit's every path runs the fallback arm these tests hold.

While the pane is open but undrawn, one line draws above the prompt carrying the word ready and an [Open] Button whose hotkey is o; the press re-opens the pane and the band then goes. The band is absent when the pane is drawn and while a survey holds the band (e.props.hasSurvey), the second read against the same waiting state as the first so the absence is the survey's doing. Tests cover the line and the Button, the press's $.ui.open, and both absences.

The press that seats the pane is an ASKING open: the $.ui.open happens inside the Button's own press (the engine places an open asked by a Button press at any width), not deferred to a timer, a later draw or another event, which would leave it unasked and undrawn at the same width. A test asserts the open arrives while the press is being handled.

The routing rule from opum-doc seq 183 is unchanged: test/plugin-skill.test.ts keeps its case sending a real CLI command word to the CLI, and no case asserting that a non-CLI word reaches the pane is added.

bun run test:mod passes with the new tests, bun test passes on the branch head, and bun run lore check exits 0 with the band and the honest result recorded in docs/reference/lore-pane-mod.md. Any workstation-only failure is named with its reachability from this diff rather than assumed.

plan: 1. Measure the design's premise in a live session (the ruling's own first step): does a band Button press seat the pane below the floor, where an unasked open does not. Measured 2026-10-03 on Claude Code 2.1.288 at 100 columns with a scratch plugin in a pty; it holds (press -> isPlaced true and the pane drawn; session.start and a model tool call -> isPlaced false with the engine's reason). Recording the transcript excerpts on this task.

2. Implement the honest result in openDashboard: read $.ui.open's UiOpenResult and confirm against $.ui.panes(), then answer for the state found -- opened when placed and shown, the engine's own reason when it waits undrawn, and behind-a-tab when placed but not shown.

3. Implement the band: a ui.render hook on AbovePrompt drawing one line and an [Open] Button (hotkey o) exactly while the pane is open and unplaced, yielding to a survey; the press calls $.ui.open in the press itself.
4. Tests in tests/pane.test.tsx: the three result arms with the placed case as control, the band's line and Button, the press's open, and the band's absences.
5. Docs: record the band and the honest result in docs/reference/lore-pane-mod.md; the skill-routing copy is untouched (seq 183).
6. Gates solo: bun run test:mod, bun test, bun run lore check; then the branch, PR and CI.
implementationNotes:
MEASUREMENT, the ruling's own first step, run before any implementation. Claude Code 2.1.288 (workstation; CI pins 2.1.287), a scratch plugin in /tmp (not this repo) driven in a real pty at 100x40 columns, its band drawing what each open answered as plain text. The answer to the ruling's question is yes, and the premise holds: a band Button press seats the pane below the floor, where an unasked open does not.

- UNSAKED, session.start, 100 columns: {"isPlaced":false,"reason":"unasked below 144 columns (100 now): placed when the person opens it, or when the terminal is widened to 144 columns"}. Nothing drawn.
- UNSAKED, a model tool call at 100 columns (the path this task is about): the same answer verbatim, and $.ui.panes() immediately after listed both panes isShown:false, isPlaced:false. So a tool-call open is UNSAKED and waits, which is the whole reason the honest result and the band exist.
- ASKED, a band Button press at 100 columns: {"isPlaced":true}; $.ui.panes() then listed {"id":"probe-pane","isShown":true,"isFocused":false,"isPlaced":true}; and the pane drew, its body visible in the frame. This is the thing the ruling asked be measured first.
- THE FLOOR IS NOT A CONSTANT, so the honest message must not hard-code one. Once the person has opened that pane id before -- in this session OR an earlier process, so the engine remembers it across sessions -- the unasked floor drops from 144 to 110: the reason then reads "unasked below 110 columns (100 now, an id the person opened before): placed when the person opens it, or when the terminal is widened to 110 columns". The engine's own reason string carries the right floor and the width now, which is why the tool should report it rather than compose its own.

Two further engine facts the band and the honest message are built on, both measured in the same session rather than read off the declaration:

- A HOTKEY LETTER NEEDS THE BAND FOCUSED. A bare o typed into an empty composer did nothing (it landed in the composer); a bare digit pressed a band Button from an empty composer (the engine's survey rule); and o pressed the Button once ctrl+x tab had given the band the keys. So the design's hotkey o stands, but a person reaching for it must first focus the band (ctrl+x tab, or a click) -- a digit is the only key that works from the composer alone. Reported to opum-agent for opum-doc, since it changes how the affordance is described, not whether it works.
- THE ENGINE'S TEST KIT CANNOT MEASURE THIS. claude plugin test has no ui.open beneath the plugins at all -- its own words: "no implementation for ui.open ... a test answers it with on('ui.open', ...)". So no unit test can exercise the floor, the placement, or isPlaced; the mod's tests can only feed the module an answer and assert what it does with it. That is why AC1 is a live-session measurement and why the tests in AC2/AC4 assert the module's side (which answer it composes, and that the press issues the open inside the press) rather than the engine's placement.
